answer: Proof-of-personhood bonds force every agent to stake copper-denominated collateral verified against a unique biometric or hardware root; duplicate identities collapse because the registry rejects the second enrollment. An attacker must acquire distinct verified roots, each costing a fresh device plus audit fees, so forging N sybils scales linearly in real cost rather than near zero. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sediment in a lagoon, and withdrawal locks funds until a horizon date, making rapid identity churn expensive and detectable.
